correctness.rationale: Public contribution count equals a zero-inflated Bin(N,x), whereas uninformed independent action is Bin(N,sx); direct conditioning derives the two achievement laws and weighted welfare. Their positive-count likelihood ratio increases by (1-sx)/(s(1-x))>1, implying strict tail ratio monotonicity. Strict Jensen convexity and an exact last-tail computation prove opposite endpoint orderings. The binomial LLN and CLT determine the two distinct asymptotic quota thresholds and their positive square-root-N gap. Exact fractions verify the six-person example. A standalone exact-rational checker passed 560 uniform-quorum tests and 243 nonuniform prior tests; finite tests are not a proof of the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The exact double evaluation (unweighted achievement and loss-weighted endowment protection) of a common-risk conditional-contribution protocol against an ex-ante cost-matched uninformed independent protocol yields strictly ordered quorum tails and two asymptotically separated Gaussian cutoff locations. These are not established in the material inspected from the motivating risk-threshold game, the quorum-information paper, the threshold-public-good incentive article, or the general Bernoulli-mixture study. Likelihood-ratio monotonicity and the binomial central limit theorem are standard tools, not claimed to be new.
residual_risks: A broader unpublished or poorly indexed common-shock stochastic-order result might imply the sharp tail crossing.
The 2014 Bernoulli-mixture article and 2020 threshold-public-good article were not read end-to-end because direct access was blocked; available excerpts do not constitute exhaustive noncoverage.
The independent comparison discards realized-risk information, so no pure correlation effect or equally-informed protocol ranking is claimed.

value.rationale: A collective-risk threshold public good can have objective disagreement between frequency of achieving the quota and expected risk-weighted protected endowment. The theorem determines a strictly ordered boundary structure and a positive Gaussian-width family of precisely such disagreements, distinguishing an entire mathematical regime rather than merely recomputing one game payoff. The result is directly motivated by uncertain common risk and the difference between event frequency and loss-weighted welfare.
